text: Talked it through with the two friends who rescued me. Went back to the beach in daylight with them the next summer, which helped a lot.
Ich habe eine Verhaltenstherapie gegen die Klaustrophobie gemacht. Teilweise hilft das, Aufzüge gehen wieder, kleine Toiletten noch nicht.

My trans friends were my first line of support. They came over, cooked for me, made me get out of bed. Without them I don't know where I'd be.

I went back to the gender-affirming therapist I had seen during my transition. She knew me and my story and could help me separate what the shaman said from what I know about myself. That was crucial. We worked on the dysphoria, the shame and the suicidal thoughts. Later I started trauma therapy with someone else who does EMDR, which helped with the intrusive memories of his hand and the tobacco smell.

I was on an antidepressant for about a year.

I reported the retreat to the platform where I found it. They removed the listing after several other complaints. I also wrote about my experience in an online community for trans people interested in psychedelics, as a warning. Many people wrote back with similar stories, which was both comforting and horrifying.

Unhelpful: a well-meaning friend who told me I should 'forgive him because he was coming from a different culture'. I'm not ready for that, and I don't think I owe it to him.

I'm doing much better. I'm dating again. But tobacco smoke still makes me feel sick.
I did a fear of flying course run by an airline, plus CBT with a psychologist. My GP gave me a small amount of diazepam for the first flight after. It worked well enough.

Ich war bei mehreren Ärzten, die alle wenig über Depersonalisation wussten. Schließlich habe ich eine Therapeutin gefunden, die sich damit auskennt. Sie hat mir geholfen, die Angst vor den Episoden zu verringern. Medikamente haben bei mir nicht geholfen. Sport und ein geregelter Tagesablauf helfen etwas. Ganz weg ist es nicht.
Spoke to my psychiatrist honestly, restarted the SSRI slowly, and saw a counsellor for a few sessions about the health anxiety.
Therapy for about a year, which focused on trust and grief. Lots of time with my sister. I avoided rivers for a while and then took walks along one with a friend. I'm dating again, carefully.

Our fire service has a peer support team, which I'd always avoided. After I froze on that call, my captain made me talk to them. They connected me with a psychologist who works with first responders, and I did a course of trauma-focused therapy. I also cut back on drinking. Talking to the other guys on the team turned out to be the best thing, a lot of them have the same boxes in their heads. I'm back on the job.

Ich habe lange niemandem davon erzählt. Erst ein Jahr später habe ich mit einer Psychologin gesprochen, die mir geholfen hat, die Nacht in der Klinik zu verarbeiten und über meine düsteren Gedanken zu sprechen. Das hat mir gutgetan.
